verdict.reason: The quoted code is present exactly as described. `visitStyledRunsInRange` (packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:48-184) re-implements every branch of `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:349-440): same-block (range-runs.ts:116-121 vs document.ts:354-363), cross-block-within-one-cell using `blockParentMap` + cell-block index span (range-runs.ts:125-153 vs document.ts:350-351,366-389), top-level cross-block with cell endpoints normalized to the parent table block over `getContextBlocks()` (range-runs.ts:155-183 vs document.ts:393-437), and the "table in a cross-block selection is styled/read whole, colSpan===0 skipped, non-recursive" rule (range-runs.ts:78-94,175-178 vs document.ts:415-429), plus the extra `tableCellRange` rectangle case (range-runs.ts:97-113). The module's own header comment ("Mirrors `Doc.applyInlineStyle` so the runs read are the runs written", range-runs.ts:46) and the design doc (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:294-320) confirm the mirroring is by hand-copy, not by a single shared traversal that the write path also drives — so read/write agreement now depends on two independent copies staying in sync, which is the drift class issue #715 targets (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:49-54). That is a duplication/approach-fit issue, a named `major` kind for this lens. It is reachable: called from view/editor.ts:1110 and :2769, view/text-editor.ts:3035, view/text-box-editor.ts:1076. No guard, no unreachability, nothing not-present. The secondary layering claim also checks out factually (range-runs.ts:21-24 imports only model modules), though repo precedent exists for model-only helpers under view/ (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:1-2), so I weigh that part lower without it changing the verdict.

verdict.reason: All four elements of the claim verify in the working tree. docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:317-320 does state that nested-table content "is never written — and reading what cannot be written re-creates the #715 trap", codifying non-styleability as intended design. packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:587-636 pins it exactly as quoted (`expect(storedInner.inlines[0].style.bold).toBeUndefined()` at :635 with the comment "Untouched: the write never descends into the nested table" at :633), and its docblock at :580-586 frames the gap as desired. Meanwhile docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:21-22 still lists "Full feature parity inside nested tables: cell merge/split, row/column insert/delete, resize, styling" as a Goal, and its Non-Goals at :30-32 (cross-page row splitting, repeating headers, drag-and-drop between levels) contain no styling exemption; I read the full file and it never records the inline-style exception nor links to docs-font-controls.md. The only refutation I could imagine (reading "styling" in the nested-tables Goal as table/cell chrome rather than inline styling) is unsupported by that document's text, so no named ground exists to drop this.

That code is not present. editor.ts:1093-1148 contains the whole function, and its run collection is a single call to the shared walk at editor.ts:1110 (`visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, ...)`), with the function's own comment at editor.ts:1081-1086 stating it uses that shared walk. finding.summary: `visitTable` recurses into nested tables but `Doc.applyInlineStyle` does not — the read set no longer equals the write set the module promises to mirror
finding.evidence: range-runs.ts's docstring states it mirrors "`Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s dispatch" so "the runs read are the runs written". `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:63-79) recurses when `cellBlock.type === 'table'`; `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s table branch (document.ts:415-428) iterates only the cell's direct blocks and skips any with `getBlockTextLength === 0`, i.e. it never descends into a nested table. For a cross-block selection containing a table that itself contains a nested table (a supported feature — docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md), the read can report 'mixed'/`false` from runs the write will not touch, so a toggle can again be unable to reach a stable state — the same failure mode as #715.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that `visitTable` in packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts recurses when `cellBlock.type === 'table'`, creating a read/write asymmetry with `Doc.applyInlineStyle`. That code is not present. `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:78-94) has no type test and no recursion; it calls `visitWholeBlock(cellBlock)` for each direct cell block, with an explicit comment stating it is "Deliberately *not* recursive" precisely to keep parity with the write path. Grep confirms the file's only `block.type === 'table'` occurrence is line 175, the top-level cross-block dispatch into `visitTable`, not a nested descent. Functionally the two sides also match: `visitWholeBlock` uses `getBlockTextLength` (model/types.ts:326-328), which sums only the block's own inlines and therefore returns 0 for a nested-table block; `visitBlockSlice`'s overlap test (range-runs.ts:61, `pos < to` with `to === 0`) then visits nothing. `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s table branch (model/document.ts:415-429) similarly iterates only direct cell blocks and skips `len === 0`. Read set equals write set for nested tables, so the described #715-style failure mode cannot arise from this code.
